claims.text: A stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure mediates the ability of lightweight high-entropy alloys to combine low density with strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
High configurational entropy suppresses the formation of detrimental phases.
A stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances mechanical strength.
A stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances resistance to degradation.
Controlled heat treatment will induce a stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
The untreated baseline alloy lacks the stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure produced by the controlled heat treatment.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater mechanical strength than the untreated baseline alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the untreated baseline alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the untreated baseline alloy.
Exposure above approximately 1000°C can destabilize the nanoscale precipitate structure and cause the hypothesis to cease to hold.
Aggressive environments such as high-velocity oxidation can destabilize the nanoscale precipitate structure and cause the hypothesis to cease to hold.
Exposure at approximately 800°C for approximately 100 hours in a controlled inert atmosphere is a proposed test condition.
Failure of the heat treatment to significantly improve all three targeted property classes relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
